page: Amazon Web Services c8g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 infrastructure and the Nitro hypervisor. The instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core, avoiding hardware multithreading contention. Cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 32 GB, providing an explicit 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Persistent local storage is absent, necessitating network-attached storage volumes for file systems, and the configuration includes no hardware accelerators. Network connectivity provides an 8 Gbps baseline throughput.

Benchmark evaluations indicate exceptional memory subsystem efficiency alongside balanced computational throughput. In uncached large-block memory operations, the server delivers 302.31 GB/sec read and 123.66 GB/sec write bandwidth, contributing to a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3108.83. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 14.35 GB/sec, placing it in the upper quartile. Standard compute metrics reflect steady middle-tier results, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 15870.0 and a multi-core stress-ng rating of 27286.64. Database operations within synthetic tests register strong throughput at 24008.08, while Redis operations manage 35.05 million operations per second.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory profile makes the c8g.4xlarge cost-efficient for workloads bounded by processor cycles rather than excessive RAM capacity. The absence of local disk requires external volume planning, which affects overall input-output latency profiles. Medium-scale language model prompt evaluation exhibits weaker relative speed at 31.15 tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated tensor acceleration. The configuration is optimal for distributed containerized microservices, Clang-based software build environments, batch transformation pipelines, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services c8g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance features 16 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, paired with 32 GB of system memory to maintain a 1:2 core-to-RAM allocation. Cache configuration consists of 64 KB L1 data, 2 MB L2, and 36 MB shared L3 caches. The instance provides 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no bundled local storage, and includes no discrete graphics processing units. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate exceptional memory bandwidth, reaching 302.31 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and achieving top-tier PassMark memory results, complemented by strong database operation scores. General multi-core compute and compilation metrics place consistently within the middle performance tier. The instance is suitable for compute-intensive distributed services, software compilation, ETL data pipelines, and high-throughput network applications.
